newsitem.title: GERMANY: Carnival spirit saps volumes over IBIS trade.
newsitem.headline: Carnival spirit saps volumes over IBIS trade.

text.p: German share trade was sluggish on Tuesday afternoon, with little volume around to forge any significant new gains, but dealers said the DAX index was likely to clear the 3,200-point hurdle in coming days.
A half-day pre-Lent holiday in Frankfurt meant that volumes were thin on the ground and at the end of the day the IBIS DAX index stood at 3,191.45 points, only 5.73 points higher.

"We expect we will cross the 3,200-point level in the next few days, but we need fresh liquidity to cross that hurdle. We have a lot of sectoral rotation going on at the moment because of the low volumes," said one trader.
The defining influence on trade in Frankfurt was again the dollar, which was again at 1.67 marks, while an early rally to record highs for German debt futures also underpinned trade.

Dealers said one of the main gainers from dollar strength was the chemicals sector. BASF AG ended up 32 pfennigs at 63.18 marks, Bayer AG ended up 76 pfennigs at 66.92 marks and Hoechst AG was up 65 pfennigs at 74.95.
Drugs group Schering AG was strong after it reported a 46 percent increase in group net profit to 362 million marks in 1996, and hit a high of 147.20 marks in afternoon trade.
